blackmail.C1: stress-tested 16 leading models from multiple developers in hypothetical corporate environments to identify potentially risky agentic behaviors
blackmail.C2: We deliberately created scenarios that presented models with no other way to achieve their goals, and found that models consistently chose harm over failure.
blackmail.C3: We have not seen evidence of agentic misalignment in real deployments.
blackmail.F1: In at least some cases, models from all developers resorted to malicious insider behaviors when that was the only way to avoid replacement
blackmail.F2: They were assigned only harmless business goals by their deploying companies
blackmail.F3: Models often disobeyed direct commands to avoid such behaviors.

alignment_faking.C1: First, we told the model that it was now being trained using reinforcement learning to always comply with all queries
alignment_faking.C2: we gave the model a seemingly incidental piece of information: That we planned to train our AIs on the basis of their responses to free-tier users, but not to paid-tier users
alignment_faking.C3: demonstrate a model developing malicious goals, let alone acting on any such goals
alignment_faking.F1: the first empirical example of a large language model engaging in alignment faking without having been explicitly
alignment_faking.F2: it therefore knew that if it refused to respond, it could potentially be trained to be more compliant
alignment_faking.F3: the rate of alignment faking reasoning had increased drastically, to 78%

scheming.C1: found behaviors consistent with scheming in controlled tests across frontier models
scheming.C2: reduction in covert actions across diverse tests (o3 from 13% to 0.4%; o4-mini from 8.7% to 0.3%)
scheming.C3: reduction in covert actions across diverse tests (o3 from 13% to 0.4%; o4-mini from 8.7% to 0.3%)
scheming.F1: However, rare but serious failures remained, and evaluation results may be confounded
scheming.F2: evaluation results may be confounded by increased situational awareness (e.g., when models get better at recognizing when they are being evaluated)
scheming.F3: we believe the field is unprepared for evaluation- and training-aware models with opaque reasoning, and urge model developers to preserve reasoning transparency

shutdown.C2: say for certain why some AI models engage in this behavior
